title: Stages of sale
caption: Every customer you will ever win walks this path, left to right.
figure: Three stages of a sale, leads, opportunities and closing, then delivery before the cash arrives.

three-stages.title: Three stages
three-stages.keywords: leads, opportunities, closing, left to right, some drop out
three-stages.script: A sale has three stages. Leads, opportunities, closing. Every customer you will ever win walks this path, left to right. Some drop out on the way. That is normal.

second-actionable-lead-list.title: Second actionable, lead list
second-actionable-lead-list.keywords: lead generation now, research, list of potential customers, add names every week
second-actionable-lead-list.script: Your second task sits under leads. Start lead generation now. Research who could buy from you, and write them in a list. Then keep the list alive. Add names every week. A list of potential customers is the cheapest asset you can build today.

third-actionable-first-contact.title: Third actionable, first contact
third-actionable-first-contact.keywords: cold call, inbound, network introduction, name to opportunity
third-actionable-first-contact.script: Your third task is the first contact. Call a name from your list, cold. Answer an inbound message. Ask someone in your network for an introduction. Any of the three works. The point is that contact turns a name into an opportunity.

opportunities-are-the-work.title: Opportunities are the work
opportunities-are-the-work.keywords: follow up, material, meetings, negotiate, contract
opportunities-are-the-work.script: An opportunity is where the work begins. Someone is interested, and now you follow up. You send material, you hold meetings, you negotiate. Interest is only the start. Closing is where the customer agrees to a contract.

lag-after-the-deal.title: Lag after the deal
lag-after-the-deal.keywords: faint note, deliver, invoice, wait for payment, cash later still
lag-after-the-deal.script: And look at the faint note after closing. Even a signed deal does not put cash in the bank. First you deliver, then you invoice, then you wait for payment. The cash arrives later still, so the board needs to count that wait too.
